text.p: Parma breathed new life into Serie A on Sunday with a 2-1 win at Perugia.
The victory narrowed Juventus's lead to four points -- but they were due to play Internazionale later.
"In terms of points, the title race is still wide open," said Parma coach Carlo Ancelotti, whose team have lost only once this year.
"But in terms of potential, Juventus cannot be caught."
Instead, Parma are setting their sights on the runners-up spot that now guarantees a European Cup place.
Parma reacted with clinical efficiency to falling behind in the 11th minute.
Within a minute, Argentine Hernan Crespo equalised with his third goal in two matches and five minutes later Massimo Crippa scored the winner with a powerful shot from the edge of the area.
Sampdoria's faltering title challenge suffered a devastating 4-0 blow at Atalanta.
The league's leading scorer Filippo Inzaghi ran riings around Sampdoria's suspect defence to claim a hat-trick and take his season's tally to 18.
Sampdoria's Yugoslav sweeper Sinisa Mihajlovic was dismissed after he threw the ball at the referee when Atalanta were given a penalty.
Sampdoria remained fourth, eight points adrift of Juventus.

Until last week's European Cup Winners' quarter-final win at Benfica, Fiorentina had failed to win in two months. And when Swede Kennet Andersson put Bologna in front in the second minute, their miserable league record looked like continuing.
Even when Fiorentina levelled with an 18th minute Francesco Baiano penalty, Aldo Firicano promptly deflected Carlo Nervo's shot into his own net to restore Bologna's lead.

But in an inspired second-half, two superb free-kicks converted first by Gabriele Batisuta, then Anselmo Robbiati, brought Fiorentina a long-awaited three-points -- marred only by the sending-off of Swede Stefan Schwarz.
French defender Vincent Candela lifted Roma into fifth place with two goals, including a dramatic 89th minute winner, in the 4-3 win over bottom-placed Verona.
Luigi Di Biagio gave Roma a third minute lead only for Filippo Maniero and Diego Caverzan to put the visitors 2-1 up by the 35th minute.
Candela and Francesco Totti managed to restore Roma's advantage by halftime but soon after the break, Pierluigi Orlandini levelled and set the stage for the dramatic finale.

Napoli fans greeted AC Milan coach Arrigo Sacchi by throwing a black rubbish bag on to the pitch. The gesture summed up Milan's visit fittingly -- a dull scoreless draw that left the champions languishing in 12th place.
